translation_notes: DCTERMS.created becomes dcterms:created and Literal("yesterday", datatype=XSD.dateTime) becomes the literal island "yesterday"^^xsd:dateTime; the ill-typed literal the test is about is written exactly as it would be in Turtle, which is the clearest win of this region

the graph.add((s, p, o)) call is KEPT as-is rather than turned into 'np.pubinfo += g{ ... }': Nanopub.pubinfo is a read-only property (verified: 'property pubinfo of Nanopub object has no setter'), so the g{}/+= idiom recommended for runs of adds is unavailable whenever the target graph is exposed through a getter - a real limitation of the += form, not of the island itself
the subject np._metadata.namespace[""] stays a Python expression (a runtime Namespace indexed with the empty local name, which no prefixed name can denote)

'from rdflib import BNode, Graph, Literal, URIRef, Dataset, DC, RDF, Namespace, DCTERMS, PROV, XSD' is dropped in the ldpy version: after the two term constructors become islands, nothing in the region uses it (in the full test module it is of course still needed)
the draft's dc/rdf/prov prefixes are unused by this region and are not declared
context shim: nanopub_ctx.py holds _minimal_valid_nanopub, copied verbatim from the source test module (tests/test_nanopub.py lines 763-773); imported identically by both sides
the nanopub package is not installed in the eval venv, so the driver puts the corpus checkout on sys.path (it imports as-is)

the region is a pytest method that never uses self, so the driver calls it with self=None; the test is self-validating (its assertions read back the literal it just added), so an incorrect term on either side would surface as an AssertionError
